sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: Indonesia's revised National Electricity Plan (RUPTL) mandates 60% of new capacity from renewables by 2030, creating a durable demand driver for solar and geothermal developers.
The upcoming carbon tax, set at IDR 30,000 per ton CO2e, will structurally increase the cost competitiveness of renewables versus coal-fired power.
Government push for domestic solar module manufacturing via the 40% local content requirement (TKDN) is creating a long-term supply chain opportunity for Indonesian climate-tech firms.
sectors.ai: Indonesia's renewables sector is underperforming US peers, but the signal is WATCH, not SELL. Focus on domestic catalysts: the new RUPTL revision mandating 60% renewable additions by 2030 and the upcoming carbon tax implementation. Position in solar and geothermal plays, as these are the government's priority sub-sectors with the strongest policy tailwinds and project pipelines.

Regulatory stability and subsidy rationalization in staples like cooking oil and sugar are creating predictable cost environments for FMCG firms, supporting earnings visibility.
sectors.ai: Indonesia's consumer sector underperformed today, dragged by domestic names, but US strength signals resilience. Watch for selective bottom-fishing in high-momentum movers like AGAR and KLIN, which may indicate niche demand recovery. Maintain WATCH for broader rotation into staples as inflation moderates.
